cards.explanation: The answer is a desolate waste. God says, "I will stretch out My hand against you and make you a desolate waste." That's not a little messy or a fixer-upper, friends. It's a waste. And in the next verse He adds that Seir's cities will become ruins.

The answer is True, and it's the line God keeps repeating. After saying He'll turn the cities into ruins, He says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD." He says it again after He makes Seir a perpetual desolation. Seir will know exactly who has been talking.

The answer is that Seir handed them over to the sword. God says Seir "…delivered the Israelites over to the sword in the time of their disaster…" I think this one is heavy, and I'm not going to joke about it. It matters that God names what was done to His people.

The answer is pursue. God says, "Since you did not hate bloodshed, it will pursue you." Seir didn't hate bloodshed, and now bloodshed isn't going anywhere without it. It's a serious line, friends, and God says it twice in verse 6.

The answer is False. Nothing in this verse says it's only for a while. God says, "I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities will not be inhabited." Perpetual doesn't come with a reopening date. And the verse ends the same way as before: "Then you will know that I am the LORD."

The answer is that the LORD was there. God says Seir made its claim "even though the LORD was there…" Seir said those lands would be its own, and the LORD was there. Bold doesn't even cover it, friends.

The answer is against God Himself. God says, "You boasted against Me with your mouth and multiplied your words against Me. I heard it Myself!" Seir's words were about Israel's mountains, but God says they were aimed at Him. He heard every one of them (Ezekiel 35:12).

The answer is rejoices. God says, "While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate." That's the timing He gives: the earth rejoices, and He makes Seir desolate. That's all the verse says about it, so I won't guess beyond it.

The answer is True. God says, "You will become a desolation, O Mount Seir, and so will all of Edom." Edom is another name for Esau, who settled in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36:8). So the word reaches past one mountain to all of Edom.
The answer is True. God says, "…they have made you desolate and have trampled you on every side…" Every side, friends. He sees the whole picture of what Israel's mountains went through.

The answer is plunder. God says Edom took His land "…with wholehearted joy and utter contempt, so that its pastureland became plunder." Wholehearted joy at taking what wasn't theirs. God hears all of it.

The answer is that they will endure reproach of their own. God says, "I have sworn with an uplifted hand that surely the nations around you will endure reproach of their own." The mountains endured reproach, and now the nations will too. And He swore it with an uplifted hand.

The answer is that they will produce branches and bear fruit, and I love this part. God says, "But you, O mountains of Israel, will produce branches and bear fruit for My people Israel…" The ruined mountains get a harvest again. And it's for His people.

The answer is True. God says the mountains will bear fruit for His people, "…for they will soon come home." Soon, friends. That comes in verse 8, right after the promise of fruit. After all that talk of ruins, it's a good word to hear.

The answer is that it will be tilled and sown. God says, "…I am on your side; I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown." Tilled means someone's working the ground again, and sown means seed is going in. And it all starts with God turning toward the mountains.

The answer is rebuilt. God says, "The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt." People will live in the cities again, and the broken places get fixed. That's the opposite of what He said about Seir.

The answer is that He will make them prosper more than before. God says, "I will make you as inhabited as you once were, and I will make you prosper more than before." Back to how it was, and then more. I think that's God being generous, and I'm leaning in again.

The answer is False. People say the land devours men, but God says, "…you will no longer devour men or deprive your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD." No longer. He's speaking to the land there, and what people say doesn't get the last word. He adds that He will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against it (Ezekiel 36:15).

The answer is the taunts of the nations. God says, "I will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against you…" The mountains were mocked by the nations around them, and God says the mocking stops. That's a promise you can hang your oven mitt on, friends.
